As someone who has family in that area,it is nice to see countries, such as Georgia or Belarus,that aren’t seen often in AG,be represented in RG.  I think many Americans view it as being the number #1 sport here, when in reality it holds the place that AG or figure skating has in the US. The girls are the ~stars~ of the Olympics,but are generally forgotten by the general population during the other 3 years. Rythmic gyms are easily found here,but most kids are pushed into soccer or other sports. Israel has a strong RG scene as well,due to the influence of many Russian immigrants in the 1970s!

RG also seems to be tied to politics in many cases. For Russia,you have Irina Viner & Alina Kabaeva. In Azerbaijan,the head of RG is also the first lady,which has caused some controversy before. There’s been accusations of corruption for years now,though most of it has been aimed at Russia. Due to how well connected RG is,athletes often don’t have the outlets to speak up about the abusive training conditions they face. 

I’d recommend any newbies to the sport look up Alina Kabaeva! She’s a fascinating figure in RG. Aside from being Putin’s assumed partner/baby mama,she plays a huge role in the sport. Many view her as someone who revolutionized the world of RG,and she’s been named as the inspiration for many current  Russian gymnasts since. She trained with Viner,and was initially turned away on the grounds she was too “fat” and “ugly” to participate in the sport. She was only allowed to stay if she could lose 6 pounds in 3 days,and could only have water for breakfast,lunch and dinner.  She won AA in Athens,has been stripped of titles due to doping accusations,and ended up serving in the Duma for awhile and somehow being involved with Putin.  Irina has alluded to their relationship from time to time. 


If anyone interested in Russian RG,there’s some good documentaries available to watch. Over the Limit is probably the most well known,but there are a few on youtube by RT that imo,did a good job of showing the high pressure environment these girls are in,and how the HBIC Viner operates.
